components.gap: Feller Vol. I (3rd ed.) II.9, pp. 52-54, which the chapter declares as its required Stirling referral "including its continuation" (body lines 11-15), is not supplied in full on the route: (i) its historical and bibliographic claims are absent: the formula is James Stirling's, Methodus differentialis, 1730 (p. 52, n. 14); the proof by d_n - d_(n+1) and the inequality (9.14) are due to H. E. Robbins, Amer. Math. Monthly 62 (1955), pp. 26-29 (p. 53, n. 15; the route only uses Robbins's name in titles and the index); the usual proof that e^C = sqrt(2 pi) relies on Wallis's formula, and Feller gives a simple direct proof in Amer. Math. Monthly (1967) (p. 53, n. 16); (ii) Feller's justificatory claim that the constant proof is elementary, independent of chapters IV-VI, and postponed to VII.2 because it is naturally connected with the normal approximation theorem (p. 53) is absent; (iii) the Refinements claims after (9.15) are absent: the ratio of the extreme members of (9.15) is close to 1 - (12n^2)^(-1), so the right-hand member overestimates n! with an error of less than 9n^(-2) per cent (p. 54; the digit carries a pen mark in the held scan). Supply these claims with Robbins's bounds.
